claim: Group free-association networks of high-creative people have shorter paths (ASPL 4.6 vs 3.93), smaller diameter (12 vs 8) and higher small-world index, from 33 vs 33 people; one study, group-level, no individual effect size. Gap search: no independent or preregistered replication found. Same-lab extensions (percolation re-analysis, 2019 proceedings) are not independent; a larger N=477 study (Luchini 2023, abstract only) points the same way for convergent thinking; Robinson 2024 finds global path length unreliable within a person.
agent_test: Seed an open-mode run with concepts at short vs long graph distance on a fixed word graph; compare originality at equal tokens.

claim: Part of the 2014 network gap is a fluency artefact: high-creative people give more unique responses (eta2=.614). With only the first 10 responses the path and spread gap persists but the modularity direction reverses.
agent_test: Equalise the number of generated candidates before comparing structure of the agent's concept graph.

claim: Mednick's flat-versus-steep gradient is not supported at the response-strength level: no group x rank interaction (F=0.98) and no slope difference (t(98)=-0.28), but creative people are more fluent and give more uncommon answers.
agent_test: Test flat vs steep by sampling many associations per seed and checking whether fluency alone (more samples) reproduces the gain.

claim: The 2018 percolation re-analysis (same 66 people) says the creative network is more robust to weak-link removal (integral 15.64 vs 14.76), and a shuffled control reverses it. It is a re-analysis, not an independent replication; authors flag small N. Numbers re-opened: percolation integral 14.76 (LSC) vs 15.64 (HSC), n=33 per group.
agent_test: None direct; a caution about reuse of one dataset.

claim: Independent individual-level data (N=101, relatedness ratings) agree in sign: more real-life creative activity and achievement go with shorter weighted paths and lower modularity, rs about -.28 to -.30. Small.
agent_test: Build a per-run relatedness graph of the agent's own concepts and test modularity against solution originality.

claim: Larger later samples find the individual-level link weak and metric-dependent: N=236 r=.14-.15; N=106 only fluency predicts originality (R2=.503); N=479 R2=.03 for AUT; N=126 omnibus p=.050-.055. Direction mostly consistent, effect small.
agent_test: Treat network shape as at most a weak predictor; do not tune the agent on it without a direct ablation.

claim: Network metrics from one person are highly redundant (global efficiency vs modularity r=-.75), so 'short paths' and 'low modularity' are about one dimension.
agent_test: Report one structure index, not many, in any agent-side test.

claim: Semantic distance from embeddings tracks human originality ratings, but strength varies by study (latent r .45 to .91) and by rater instruction; it measures novelty, not usefulness (r with appropriateness -.81 in one study). Metric choice matters: an LLM-embedding DAT correlates r=.65 with the GloVe DAT and has slightly lower AUT validity.
agent_test: Use embedding distance of seed-to-answer as a cheap novelty proxy, always paired with a usefulness check.

claim: Distance of word associations also predicts learning of new words (r=.33 day 1, .38 day 2, N about 142) after controlling intelligence.
agent_test: Low priority for the agent.

claim: DAT validity is modest and sample dependent: screened r=.50 vs full .32 for AUT originality in small studies, but the preregistered N=8,572 study gave r=.13. Re-opened: Study 1A N=141 screened r=.50 vs full .32, replicated in Study 1B N=285 (r=.32), retest r=.73 (N=50).
agent_test: Do not use DAT score alone as a creativity target for the agent.

claim: Top LLMs beat the average human on the DAT: GPT-4 greedy 89.1 (above 96.1% of humans), GPT-3.5-turbo 80.8; GPT-4 is above the human mean but below highly creative people in a 100,000-person comparison.
agent_test: Baseline: measure DAT distance of agent seed sets with and without O7 at equal tokens.

claim: LLM distance is instruction driven: without the DAT prompt models give related words; a strategy hint (etymology, thesaurus) raises scores; naming opposites lowers them because opposites are close in embedding space.
agent_test: Test strategy-named seed instructions ('vary etymology') against plain 'be far' at equal tokens.

claim: LLM far-word sets are repetitive: GPT-4 puts microscope in 70% and elephant in 60% of sets; GPT-4-turbo puts ocean in over 90%; humans' top word is car at 1.4%. Across-run diversity is low even when distance is high.
agent_test: Count distinct seeds across independent runs; force exclusion lists of previously used seeds.

claim: Temperature or top-p raises DAT for weaker models but harms stability; GPT-4 gains nothing from sampling. Newer models are not automatically better (GPT-4-turbo below GPT-4).
agent_test: Prefer explicit distance instructions plus exclusion lists over higher temperature.

claim: Cross-model homogeneity is rising: AUT cross-family cosine distance fell from about 0.50 to under 0.40 across 68 models; same-prompt similarity above 0.8 in 79% of cases in a 70+ model study. Diversity decoding does not fix it.
agent_test: Measure pairwise similarity of the agent's own repeated runs; test persona or role seeding at equal tokens.

claim: Persona-set conditioning widens LLM output diversity (AUT diversity +78.8%, homogeneity 0.946 to 0.798) while DAT barely moves (89.13 to 89.48). A second study (Ibrahim 2026) finds a population-referential instruction lifts diversity 0.04 to 0.06 at 1.1x tokens.
agent_test: Test persona-seeded open mode against none at equal tokens.

claim: The Mednick/Kenett mapping fails for an LLM: GPT-4o has longer paths (4.378 vs 3.33), higher modularity and a more fragile network than both human groups, yet beats low-creative humans on originality. Bootstrap method inflates the human gap.
agent_test: Do not use graph shape of the model's outputs as a creativity target; use output-level distance only.

claim: LLM free-association networks differ from human ones: fewer unique responses (Haiku 15,275 vs humans 116,640), lower degree for Haiku, fewer than half of nodes shared, edge overlap 13-23%, with similar priming effects.
agent_test: Do not treat LLM associations as human-like norms; use an external graph or embedding for distance.

claim: Free association read out from LLMs is a noisy readout of their hidden geometry (RSA r=.14 vs .35-.46 for forced choice).
agent_test: Measure seed distance by forced choice or embedding, not by asking the model to free-associate.

claim: Association-chain distance (PACE) correlates with creative-writing rank (Spearman .739, 30 models), but the source is anonymous and sensitive to embedding choice (GloVe .529 vs MUSE .757).
agent_test: Use chain-length distance as a diagnostic only.

claim: Distance alone ignores appropriateness: several top LLMs fall below trivial baselines on DAT-type scores in a conditional version, and a random WordNet sampler beats most humans on the DAT. Liu 2026: originality vs feasibility r=-.74; human top ideas lose utility, LLM top ideas do not.
agent_test: Always score distance together with fit to the task at equal tokens.

claim: Weight steering raises DAT by up to 14 human percentile points in small open models and cuts top-10 word share by 10.2 points; originality gain d=+0.40 (human N=720). Needs weights, so not applicable to a scaffold-only agent.
agent_test: Out of scope.

claim: Human ideas far from an AI idea pool were not rated worse and more distinctive ones got higher ratings; LLM alignment with default-mode brain activity rises with idea originality (N=170).
agent_test: Use pool-distance filtering: reject candidates too close to the agent's own earlier candidates.

claim: Schooling-type structure changes are tiny: Montessori vs traditional children differ by d=0.24 (path) and 0.32 (modularity) with creativity d=0.58; quasi-experimental.
agent_test: None.

claim: Search structure matters beyond network shape: clustering in verbal search predicts AUT fluency and uniqueness, switching is tied to executive control, and path-dependent search models fit human lists better than pure random walks.
agent_test: Test cluster-then-switch seed ordering against random seed order.

claim: For LLMs the benefit of a supplied far concept depends on distance and model strength: only the two best models (o3, Claude-Sonnet-4) gained from a random source, and only in the top 50% (beta=.12) or top 10% (beta=.24) most distant pairs; all pairs gave beta=.02 (n.s.). Humans gained at nearly every distance.
agent_test: Run the same open-mode task with seeds at graded distances (bottom, middle, top decile) and compare originality and correctness at equal tokens, for a strong and a weaker model.

claim: For humans, always-far inspirations do not beat near or no inspirations: novelty of best ideas 0.64 vs 0.88 with none, slower ideation, less within-category search (N=245). Far helps at an impasse, near while productive (SIAM). Liu 2026 finds humans do benefit from a far source in a different task, so the effect depends on task and how the far concept is supplied.
agent_test: Gate far seeds on a detected impasse (cluster exhausted) versus always-on, and compare.

claim: Distance buys novelty at a cost to feasibility: across ideas originality and feasibility correlate r=-.74. Top 10% human cross-domain ideas lose utility (beta=.81) while equally original LLM ideas do not, because LLMs transfer structure and function, not surface features.
agent_test: Always add a fit and usefulness check after a far-seed idea; measure feasibility alongside originality.

claim: No study has tested the upper end of seed distance. Existing dose-response data (Liu 2026) rise monotonically to the top 10% most distant pairs and cannot show or exclude an inverted U; no study varies distance randomly and measures usefulness or correctness. Gap 4 stays open.
agent_test: Add a far-end bin (unrelated domain) to the dose-response run and watch correctness.

claim: Global semantic-network metrics are not stable within a person across relatedness tasks (path length r from -.08 to .53, mostly not above a permutation null; N=70 x 4 experiments), while local pairwise relatedness is reliable. Distance for the agent should be pairwise, not a graph statistic.
agent_test: Use pairwise seed-to-problem relatedness from one calibrated embedding.

claim: Cheap diversification exists at near-equal tokens: verbalized sampling (one call, k answers with probabilities) raises creative diversity 1.6 to 2.1 times, and a one-call planning split into semantic directions gives the best diversity gain per 100k tokens (0.21 to 0.38) with quality proxies preserved. Exclusion lists and persona seeding at equal tokens with correctness were not tested.
agent_test: Compare verbalized sampling, direction planning and a plain exclusion list at equal tokens on a task with a checkable answer.

claim: Across LLMs, more flexible search (more jumps between semantic categories) goes with higher originality (observational); humans show no such link and temperature does not change the profile. No study forces a cluster-then-switch order on an LLM. Gap 7 stays open.
agent_test: Prompt for k ideas per cluster then a forced jump, versus random order, at equal tokens.

claim: Remote association is a model-level skill that predicts other creative skills: across 35 LLMs association originality correlates r=.73 with analogy originality and .42 to .50 with blend scores; humans (N=75) score below nearly every LLM.
agent_test: Use a short remote-association probe to choose which model runs open mode.
